# Owned ASAR inputs

`scripts/generate-asar-fixtures.py --reference <pinned-reference-root> [--check]` invokes the owned `reference.mjs` adapter against the author's public API. The reference is the npm package `@electron/asar` [v4.3.2](https://github.com/electron/asar/releases/tag/v4.3.2), under local `build/toolchain/references/asar-4.3.2/`. The downloaded package SHA-256 is `0408087c32787a8da57177c7f78565d169b8089f0df1e96580f3a33e71d8acb8`; its npm SHA-512 integrity is checked before comparing every installed package file with the fixed archive. No reference implementation or package dependency enters the product or Git.

`ordinary.asar` is generated by the author tool, with `assets/资料.txt`, an empty directory, `hello.txt`, an empty file and `copy.txt`. The two text copies contain `abracadabra abracadabra\n` repeated six times and share a stored offset. The UTF-8 file contains `owned UTF-8 ASAR content\n资料\n`. Every file is independently extracted and compared with the owned original bytes. Names and stream order are fixed; no archive contents are executed.

The adapter constructs six additional small profiles from the published Pickle/JSON layout and independently reads them with the author API. `without-integrity.asar` removes optional declarations while preserving the ordinary payload. `shared.asar` stores the phrase once for two identities and declares 64-byte SHA-256 blocks. `executable.asar` declares the executable flag on the phrase's `run.txt`, without executing or restoring that permission. `external.asar` declares one unpacked file, and `link.asar` declares one link plus its stored target. External and link metadata are inspected with link following disabled; no adjacent external file is supplied or read. `empty.asar` contains an empty tree. The presence of unsupported-profile inputs is not a product support claim. Reports remain under `build/`.
